newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures up amid sterling strength.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures up amid sterling strength.

text.p: A rise in the value of sterling pushed LIFFE wheat futures down, traders said.
The main volume in the market came from people rolling positions out of March and into May and July, but mainly May, one trader said.
"That's where most of the volume came from," he said.
It meant that March and May dominated volume with 193 lots of March and 193 lots of May traded out of a total wheat volume of 461 lots.
March, last traded 0.35 stg lower at 93.45 stg. May last traded 0.50 stg lower at 95.70 stg.
Barley was largely ignored with just 17 lots traded, 9 of them on May, the most active month. May last traded up 0.25 stg at 95.00 stg.
The pound zoomed higher against the mark on Tuesday, capitalising from concern about whether Italy, Spain and other "peripherals" will join the first wave of European monetary union (EMU).
Sterling also had a good run against the French franc.
